name: Lance
special: You have disadvantage when you use a lance to attack a target within 5 feet of you. Also, a lance requires two hands to wield when you are not mounted.

name: Net
special: A Large or smaller creature hit by a net is restrained until it is freed. A net has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a DC 10 Strength check to free itself or another creature within its reach, ending the effect on a success. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the net (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it. When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a net, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

name: Padded Armor
desc: Quilted layers of cloth and batting. Cheap, but rustles loudly.

name: Leather Armor
desc: A breastplate and shoulder protectors of leather stiffened by boiling in oil, with softer materials covering the rest.

name: Studded Leather Armor
desc: Tough but flexible leather reinforced with close-set rivets or spikes.

name: Hide Armor
desc: Crude armor of thick furs and pelts, common among barbarian tribes and frontier folk.

name: Chain Shirt
desc: Interlocking metal rings worn between layers of clothing or leather. Protects the torso while staying quiet under outer garments.

name: Scale Mail
desc: A coat and leggings of leather covered with overlapping pieces of metal, much like the scales of a fish.

name: Breastplate
desc: A fitted metal chest piece worn with supple leather, leaving the limbs relatively unencumbered.

name: Half Plate
desc: Shaped metal plates covering most of the body, with simple greaves held by leather straps. No helmet visor or full leg protection.

name: Ring Mail
desc: Leather armor with heavy rings sewn into it. Inferior to chain mail — usually worn by those who can afford nothing better.

name: Chain Mail
desc: Interlocking metal rings over a layer of quilted fabric, including gauntlets.

name: Splint Armor
desc: Narrow vertical strips of metal riveted to a leather backing worn over cloth padding, with flexible chain mail at the joints.

name: Plate Armor
desc: Shaped, interlocking metal plates covering the entire body, with a gambeson beneath and buckles distributing the weight.

name: Shield
desc: Made from wood or metal and carried in one hand. Wielding a shield increases your Armor Class by 2. You can benefit from only one shield at a time.

name: Acid (vial)
desc: As an action, you can splash or throw this vial up to 20 feet. On a hit (ranged attack), the target takes 2d6 acid damage.

name: Alchemist’s Fire (flask)
desc: Sticky, adhesive fluid that ignites when exposed to air. Thrown up to 20 feet; on a hit the target takes 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of its turns until it douses the flames (DC 10 Dexterity check as an action).

name: Arrows (20)
desc: Ammunition for bows. Sold in bundles of twenty.

name: Crossbow Bolts (20)
desc: Ammunition for crossbows. Sold in cases of twenty.

name: Sling Bullets (20)
desc: Smooth stones or lead pellets for a sling. Sold in pouches of twenty.

name: Blowgun Needles (50)
desc: Thin needles fired from a blowgun, often coated with poison.

name: Antitoxin (vial)
desc: A creature that drinks this vial of liquid gains advantage on saving throws against poison for 1 hour.

name: Backpack
desc: A leather pack with straps. Holds up to 1 cubic foot or 30 pounds of gear.

name: Ball Bearings (bag of 1,000)
desc: As an action, spill these to cover a level 10-foot-square area. A creature moving across must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity save or fall prone (half-speed movement avoids the save).

name: Bedroll
desc: A padded sleeping roll for camping in the wild.

name: Bell
desc: A small brass bell. Handy for improvised alarms.

name: Blanket
desc: A thick woolen blanket against cold nights.

name: Block and Tackle
desc: A set of pulleys with rope and hook. Lets you hoist up to four times the weight you can normally lift.

name: Book
desc: A book of lore, poetry, history, or any other subject. Blank books are useful as journals.

name: Bottle, Glass
desc: Holds 1½ pints of liquid.

name: Caltrops (bag of 20)
desc: As an action, spread to cover a 5-foot square. A creature entering the area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity save or stop moving and take 1 piercing damage, reducing its speed by 10 feet until it regains at least 1 hit point.

name: Candle
desc: Sheds bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet, for 1 hour.

name: Case, Map or Scroll
desc: A waterproof leather tube holding up to ten rolled sheets of paper or five sheets of parchment.

name: Chain (10 feet)
desc: Has 10 hit points. Can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength check.

name: Chalk (1 piece)
desc: For marking passages, doors, and dungeon walls so you can find your way back.

name: Chest
desc: A sturdy wooden strongbox holding 12 cubic feet or 300 pounds of gear.

name: Climber’s Kit
desc: Includes pitons, boot tips, gloves, and a harness. As an action, anchor yourself so you can’t fall more than 25 feet from the anchor point.

name: Clothes, Common
desc: Sturdy everyday wear for labourers and townsfolk.

name: Clothes, Fine
desc: Expensive garments suited to nobility and high society.

name: Clothes, Traveler’s
desc: Boots, breeches, shirt, and cloak made for life on the road.

name: Component Pouch
desc: A small watertight pouch holding all the material components needed for your spells (except those with a listed cost).

name: Crowbar
desc: Using a crowbar grants advantage on Strength checks where its leverage can be applied.

name: Fishing Tackle
desc: A wooden rod, silken line, corkwood bobbers, steel hooks, lead sinkers, velvet lures, and netting.

name: Flask or Tankard
desc: Holds 1 pint of liquid.

name: Grappling Hook
desc: A steel hook for catching ledges and battlements; attach a rope to scale walls.

name: Hammer
desc: For driving pitons, nails, and tent stakes.

name: Hammer, Sledge
desc: A heavy two-handed hammer for breaking stone and demolition.

name: Healer’s Kit
desc: Bandages, salves, and splints; ten uses. As an action, expend one use to stabilize a creature at 0 hit points without a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

name: Holy Symbol (amulet)
desc: An amulet depicting a deity’s symbol. A cleric or paladin can use it as a spellcasting focus.

name: Holy Water (flask)
desc: As an action, splash or throw up to 20 feet. On a hit, a fiend or undead takes 2d6 radiant damage.

name: Hourglass
desc: Measures the passage of one hour of sand.

name: Hunting Trap
desc: A saw-toothed steel ring that snaps shut on a DC 13 Dexterity save failure, dealing 1d4 piercing damage and stopping movement. Escape requires a DC 13 Strength check.

name: Ink (1-ounce bottle)
desc: Black ink for writing. Enough for a great deal of correspondence.

name: Ink Pen
desc: A wooden stick with a metal nib, dipped in ink to write.

name: Ladder (10-foot)
desc: A simple wooden ladder. Awkward to carry, invaluable in a pit.

name: Lamp
desc: Casts bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Burns 6 hours on a flask of oil.

name: Lantern, Bullseye
desc: Casts bright light in a 60-foot cone and dim light for an additional 60 feet. Burns 6 hours on a flask of oil.

name: Lantern, Hooded
desc: Casts bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Burns 6 hours per flask of oil. As an action, lower the hood to reduce it to dim light in a 5-foot radius.

name: Lock
desc: Comes with a key. Without the key, a creature proficient with thieves’ tools can pick it with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check.

name: Magnifying Glass
desc: Grants advantage on ability checks made to appraise or inspect small, highly detailed items. Can light a fire with sunlight, tinder, and 5 minutes.

name: Manacles
desc: Restrain a Small or Medium creature. Escaping requires a DC 20 Dexterity check; breaking them requires a DC 20 Strength check. 15 hit points; comes with one key.

name: Mess Kit
desc: A tin box containing a cup and simple cutlery; clamps together as a cooking pan and shallow plate.

name: Mirror, Steel
desc: A polished steel hand mirror. Useful for peering around corners — or facing things best not looked at directly.

name: Oil (flask)
desc: Thrown as a splash weapon (5 fire damage if lit within 1 minute of hitting), or poured to cover a 5-foot-square area (5 fire damage for entering the burning area). Also fuels lamps and lanterns for 6 hours.

name: Paper (one sheet)
desc: A sheet of fine paper for letters and maps.

name: Parchment (one sheet)
desc: Treated hide for documents and spell scrolls.

name: Perfume (vial)
desc: A fragrant vial — useful for impressing nobles or masking less pleasant smells.

name: Pick, Miner’s
desc: A heavy pick for breaking rock and digging through rubble.

name: Piton
desc: An iron spike hammered into rock or wood to anchor a rope.

name: Poison, Basic (vial)
desc: Coats one slashing or piercing weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution save or take 1d4 poison damage. Dries after 1 minute.

name: Pole (10-foot)
desc: The classic dungeon-delver’s tool for prodding suspicious floors and triggering traps from a distance.

name: Pot, Iron
desc: Holds 1 gallon of liquid. For stews, soups, and improvised helmets.

name: Potion of Healing
desc: A vial of glimmering red liquid. A character who drinks it regains 2d4 + 2 hit points. Drinking or administering a potion takes an action.

name: Pouch
desc: A cloth or leather pouch holding up to 1/5 cubic foot or 6 pounds of gear.

name: Quiver
desc: Holds up to 20 arrows.

name: Ram, Portable
desc: Grants a +4 bonus on Strength checks to break down doors. Another character helping gives you advantage as well.

name: Rations (1 day)
desc: Dry travel food: jerky, hardtack, dried fruit, and nuts. One day’s sustenance.

name: Robes
desc: Loose, flowing garments favoured by wizards, priests, and the dramatically inclined.

name: Rope, Hempen (50 feet)
desc: Has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

name: Rope, Silk (50 feet)
desc: Lighter and stronger than hemp. Has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

name: Sack
desc: A cloth sack holding up to 1 cubic foot or 30 pounds of gear.

name: Shovel
desc: For digging camps, latrines, and the occasional shallow grave.

name: Signal Whistle
desc: A shrill whistle audible from a long way off — perfect for alarms and signals.

name: Signet Ring
desc: A ring engraved with a personal seal, pressed into wax to mark documents.

name: Soap
desc: For the rare adventurer who values hygiene.

name: Spellbook
desc: A leather-bound tome with 100 blank vellum pages, essential for wizards recording their spells.

name: Spikes, Iron (10)
desc: Heavy spikes for wedging doors shut (or open) and anchoring ropes.

name: Spyglass
desc: Objects viewed through a spyglass are magnified to twice their size.

name: Tent, Two-Person
desc: A simple portable canvas shelter that sleeps two.

name: Tinderbox
desc: Flint, fire steel, and tinder. Lighting a torch or exposed fuel takes an action; anything else takes 1 minute.

name: Torch
desc: Burns for 1 hour, casting bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. As an improvised melee weapon it deals 1 fire damage on a hit.

name: Vial
desc: Holds 4 ounces of liquid.

name: Waterskin
desc: Holds 4 pints of liquid. A day’s water for one traveller in temperate climes.

name: Whetstone
desc: For keeping blades keen around the campfire.

name: Alchemist’s Supplies
desc: Glass beakers, a metal frame, a glass stirring rod, mortar and pestle, and common alchemical ingredients. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to craft alchemical substances or identify them.

name: Brewer’s Supplies
desc: A large glass jug, hops, a siphon, and tubing for brewing ale and detecting spoiled drink.

name: Calligrapher’s Supplies
desc: Ink, a dozen sheets of parchment, and three quills for fine penmanship and identifying forgeries.

name: Carpenter’s Tools
desc: A saw, hammer, nails, hatchet, square, ruler, adze, plane, and chisel for working wood.

name: Cartographer’s Tools
desc: A quill, ink, parchment, compass, calipers, and ruler for making accurate maps.

name: Cobbler’s Tools
desc: A hammer, awl, knife, lasting stand, cutter, spare leather, and thread for making and repairing footwear.

name: Cook’s Utensils
desc: A metal pot, knives, forks, stirring spoon, and ladle for preparing memorable meals.

name: Glassblower’s Tools
desc: A blowpipe, small marver, blocks, and tweezers for shaping molten glass.

name: Jeweler’s Tools
desc: A small saw, hammer, files, pliers, and tweezers for cutting gems and appraising jewellery.

name: Leatherworker’s Tools
desc: A knife, small mallet, edger, hole punch, thread, and leather scraps for crafting leather goods.

name: Mason’s Tools
desc: A trowel, hammer, chisel, brushes, and square for working stone.

name: Painter’s Supplies
desc: An easel, canvas, paints, brushes, charcoal sticks, and a palette for painting and drawing.

name: Potter’s Tools
desc: Potter’s needles, ribs, scrapers, a knife, and calipers for shaping clay.

name: Smith’s Tools
desc: Hammers, tongs, charcoal, rags, and a whetstone for forging and repairing metal gear.

name: Tinker’s Tools
desc: A variety of hand tools, thread, needles, whetstone, leather scraps, and metal fittings for mending mundane objects.

name: Weaver’s Tools
desc: Thread, needles, and scraps of cloth for weaving and repairing textiles.

name: Woodcarver’s Tools
desc: A knife, gouge, and small saw for carving wood into useful or beautiful shapes.

name: Disguise Kit
desc: Cosmetics, hair dye, and small props. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to create a visual disguise.

name: Forgery Kit
desc: Papers, parchments, pens, inks, seals, sealing wax, gold and silver leaf. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to create physical forgeries.

name: Herbalism Kit
desc: Clippers, mortar and pestle, pouches, and vials. Proficiency lets you identify or apply herbs, and create antitoxin and potions of healing.

name: Navigator’s Tools
desc: A sextant, compass, calipers, ruler, parchment, ink, and quill. Proficiency lets you chart a ship’s course and avoid becoming lost at sea.

name: Poisoner’s Kit
desc: Vials, chemicals, and other equipment. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to craft or handle poisons.

name: Thieves’ Tools
desc: A small file, lock picks, a small mirror on a handle, narrow-bladed scissors, and pliers. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to disarm traps or open locks.

name: Dice Set
desc: A set of gaming dice. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to play games with them.

name: Playing Card Set
desc: A deck of playing cards. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to play games with them.

name: Bagpipes
desc: A reeded windbag instrument. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to play music with it; bards can use it as a spellcasting focus.

name: Drum
desc: A hand drum. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to play music with it; bards can use it as a spellcasting focus.

name: Flute
desc: A simple woodwind. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to play music with it; bards can use it as a spellcasting focus.

name: Horn
desc: A brass or animal horn. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to play music with it; bards can use it as a spellcasting focus.

name: Lute
desc: The classic bard’s stringed instrument. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to play music with it; bards can use it as a spellcasting focus.

name: Lyre
desc: A small stringed harp. Proficiency lets you add your bonus to checks made to play music with it; bards can use it as a spellcasting focus.

name: Burglar’s Pack
desc: Everything the discerning second-storey specialist needs for a night’s work.

name: Dungeoneer’s Pack
desc: Provisions and hardware for delving deep below the surface.

name: Explorer’s Pack
desc: The standard kit for long overland journeys — the most popular starting pack.

name: Priest’s Pack
desc: Ritual supplies and travel gear for the devoted servant of a deity.

name: Scholar’s Pack
desc: Writing implements and reference material for the academically inclined.
